1.word_for_word: ततस् तु सप्ततितमे कृष्णस्याह्निक-कर्मणि । — Then, on the seventy-seventh day of the month, Lord Kṛṣṇa performed His daily rituals.; दूत-नारदयोः कार्ये कार्य-मन्त्र-विचारणम् ॥ — The messenger and the Nārada should consider the work and the mantras of the work.; जगन्-मङ्गल-चारित्र माह्निकं जगद् ईशितुः । — The universal auspicious character is the monthly character of the Lord of the universe.; नारदेन क्वचित् किञ्चिद् दृष्टम् आह यथा-क्रमम् ॥ — Once Nārada had seen something, he described it in detail.; अथेति, इत्य् अर्थ-काम-धर्मेषु कृष्णेन श्रद्धितात्मना इति प्रस्तुतस्य श्री-कृष्णस्याह्निकस्याधिकारेऽथ-शब्दः । — Atheti, is the word atha in the authority of the daily ritual of Lord Kṛṣṇa, which is presented as the soul faithful to Kṛṣṇa in the dharmas of meaning, desire and desire.; उपवृत्तायाम् आसन्नायाम् । — in the approaching circle.; पतिभिः श्री-कृष्णैः माधव्यो माधवस्य भार्याः ॥१॥ — The husbands of Sri Krishna are the wives of Madhava.
1.translation: Then, on the seventy-seventh day of the month, Lord Kṛṣṇa performed His daily rituals. The messenger and the Nārada should consider the work and the mantras of the work. The universal auspicious character is the monthly character of the Lord of the universe. Once Nārada had seen something, he described it in detail. Atheti, is the word atha in the authority of the daily ritual of Lord Kṛṣṇa, which is presented as the soul faithful to Kṛṣṇa in the dharmas of meaning, desire and desire. in the approaching circle. The husbands of Sri Krishna are the wives of Madhava.

2.word_for_word: वन्दिन इव श्री-कृष्णं बोधयन्ति सन्ति वयांसि पक्षिणोऽरूरुवन् अति-शयेनाकूजन् । — There are birds climbing and chirping in their overlying beds, awakening Lord Kṛṣṇa like worshippers.; मन्दार-वन-वायुभिर् गायत्स्व् अलिष्व् अनिद्राणि निद्रा-रहितानि वयांसि ॥२॥ — The birds of the Mandara forest are singing in the winds of the forest, and they are sleepless.
2.translation: There are birds climbing and chirping in their overlying beds, awakening Lord Kṛṣṇa like worshippers. The birds of the Mandara forest are singing in the winds of the forest, and they are sleepless.

3.word_for_word: वैदर्भीत्य् उपलक्षणम् । — Vaidarbhi is a sub-characteristic.; परिरम्भण-विश्लेषात् तं पर्यालोच्य ॥ — From the analysis of the embrace, he looked at him.; ३-४ ॥ — 3-4
3.translation: Vaidarbhi is a sub-characteristic. From the analysis of the embrace, he looked at him. 3-4

5.word_for_word: एकम् अक्षण्डम् । — One is inexhaustible.; तत्र हेतुः, अनन्यं निरुपाधिम् । — There is a reason, exclusive and unconditional.; अत एवाव्ययं नित्यम् । — That is why the infinitive is eternal.; स्वयं-ज्योतिष्ट्वे हेतुः, नित्य-निरस्तं, नित्य-निवृत्तं कल्मषम् अविद्या यस्मात् तम् । — The cause of self-luminousness, the eternally rejected, eternally withdrawn impurity from which ignorance arises.; उपलक्षणम् आह---अस्येति । — The sub-characteristic is argued to be its.; अस्य विश्वस्य । — of this universe.; लक्षित-भावश् चासौ निर्वृतिश् च । — The marked feeling is also the satisfaction.; भावः सत्ता । — Being is being.; निर्वृतिर् आनन्दः । — Nirvṛti is bliss.; तथा हि, गुण-क्षोभात् पूर्वं सत्तामात्रं यः, सद् एव सोम्येदम् अग्र आसीत् इत्य्-आदि-श्रुतेः । — Thus, before the disturbance of the modes, the only entity, the Sad, was before this Soma, according to the scriptures.; स एवानन्दश् च, विज्ञानम् आनन्दम् इत्य्-आदि-श्रुतेः । — That is also bliss, according to the scriptures, “Knowledge is bliss.”; तं सद् आनन्दम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥५॥ — That is, the true bliss.
5.translation: One is inexhaustible. There is a reason, exclusive and unconditional. That is why the infinitive is eternal. The cause of self-luminousness, the eternally rejected, eternally withdrawn impurity from which ignorance arises. The sub-characteristic is argued to be its. of this universe. The marked feeling is also the satisfaction. Being is being. Nirvṛti is bliss. Thus, before the disturbance of the modes, the only entity, the Sad, was before this Soma, according to the scriptures. That is also bliss, according to the scriptures, “Knowledge is bliss.” That is, the true bliss.

6.word_for_word: आप्लुतः स्नातः सन्ध्याया उपगम उपासनम् आदिर् यथा भवति तथा क्रिया-कलापं चकार, काण्वत्वाद् उदयात् पूर्वम् एव हुतानलम् । — After taking a bath, he performed the rituals as the evening approached, worshiped and began, and because he was a Kanva, he lit the fire just before sunrise.; ब्रह्म गायत्रीं जजाप ॥६॥ — He chanted the Brahma Gayatri.
6.translation: After taking a bath, he performed the rituals as the evening approached, worshiped and began, and because he was a Kanva, he lit the fire just before sunrise. He chanted the Brahma Gayatri.

7.word_for_word: कला अंशान् देवान् ऋषीन् पितॄंश् च तर्पयित्वा ॥७॥ — Kala satisfied the parts of the gods, sages and ancestors.
7.translation: Kala satisfied the parts of the gods, sages and ancestors.

8.word_for_word: गृष्टीनां प्रथम-प्रसूतानाम् ॥८॥ — The first-born of the Grishtis.

9.word_for_word:
बद्वम् इति--- — Badvam is; > हिरण्येन परीवृतान् कृष्णान् शुक्ल-दतो मृगान् । — > They saw black deer with white teeth covered in gold.; >
> मष्णारे भरतोऽददाच् छतं बद्वानि सप्त च ॥ — >
> Bharata gave Maṣṇara a roof and seven badvas.; इति श्रुत्य्-उक्तानि सप्तोत्तर-शतं बद्वान् एकी-कृत्य पुराणे चतुर्दश-लक्षत्वेन गणितानि । — Thus, the 177 Badvans mentioned in the Śrutis are counted in the Purāṇas as fourteen lakhs.; यथोक्तं भरतम् एवाधिकृत्य नवम-स्कन्धे--- — As stated in the ninth chapter, referring to Bharata himself; > मृगान् शुक्ल-दतः कृष्णान् सुवर्णेन परिष्कृतान् । — > Deer with white teeth and black teeth adorned with gold.; >
> अदात् कर्मणि मष्णारे नियुतानि चतुर्दश ॥ — >
> He gave fourteen million to the Maṣṇara for the work.; इति । — It is.; ततश् चेयं बद्व-सङ्ख्या श्लोकेन सङ्गृह्यते--- — Then this number of badvas is collected by the verse; > चतुर्दशानां लक्षाणां सप्ताधिक-शतांशकः । — > More than seven percent of the fourteen lakhs.; >
> बद्वं चतुरशीत्य्-अग्र-सहस्राणि त्रयोदश ॥ — >
> Badvam eighty-four-first thousand thirteen.; इति । — It is.; दिने दिने च प्रतिगृहं चेति ॥९॥ — day by day and every household.
9.translation:
Badvam is > They saw black deer with white teeth covered in gold. >
> Bharata gave Maṣṇara a roof and seven badvas. Thus, the 177 Badvans mentioned in the Śrutis are counted in the Purāṇas as fourteen lakhs. As stated in the ninth chapter, referring to Bharata himself > Deer with white teeth and black teeth adorned with gold. >
> He gave fourteen million to the Maṣṇara for the work. It is. Then this number of badvas is collected by the verse > More than seven percent of the fourteen lakhs. >
> Badvam eighty-four-first thousand thirteen. It is. day by day and every household.

10.word_for_word: आत्म-सम्भूतीः स-विभूतीः । — They are self-born and co-glorious.; मङ्गलानि कपिलादीनि ॥१०॥ — The auspicious ones are Kapila and others.
10.translation: They are self-born and co-glorious. The auspicious ones are Kapila and others.

11.word_for_word: नर-लोकस्य विभूषण-रूपम् आत्मानम् । — The self is the ornament of the human world.; स्वीयैः पीताम्बर-कौस्तुभादिभिः ॥११॥ — with their own yellow robes and Kaustubha gems.
11.translation: The self is the ornament of the human world. with their own yellow robes and Kaustubha gems.

12.word_for_word: कामान् अभिलषितान् अर्हान् ॥१२॥ — desires desired and worthy.

13.word_for_word: विप्रादीन् स्राग्-आदिभिः संविभज्य । — He divided the brāhmaṇas and others into garlands and other objects.; तेभ्यस् तानि दत्त्वेत्य् अर्थः । — That means giving them to them.; उपायुङ्क्त भोगार्थम् अग्रहीत् ॥१३-१४॥ — He used it and took it for pleasure.13-1
13.translation: He divided the brāhmaṇas and others into garlands and other objects. That means giving them to them. He used it and took it for pleasure.13-1

15.word_for_word: पाणी कृतेञ्जलौ गृहीत्वा ॥१५॥ — Holding his hands in his palms.
15.translation: Holding his hands in his palms.

16.word_for_word: स-व्रीड-प्रेम-वीक्षितैर् ईक्षितः क्षणं स्थितस् ताभिर् एव वीक्षितैः कृच्छ्राद् विसृष्टो निरगाद् इति ॥१६॥ — He remained there for a moment as they looked at him with shy and loving glances and with great difficulty he was released and went out.
16.translation: He remained there for a moment as they looked at him with shy and loving glances and with great difficulty he was released and went out.

17.word_for_word: एवं सर्व-गृहेभ्यः पृथक् पृथङ् निर्गत्यानन्तरम् एक एव सन् सुधर्मां प्राविशत् । — Thus, after leaving all the houses separately, he entered the Sudharma alone.; यन् निविष्टानां यत्र प्रविष्टानाम् ॥१७॥ — That which they have entered and where they have entered.
17.translation: Thus, after leaving all the houses separately, he entered the Sudharma alone. That which they have entered and where they have entered.

18.word_for_word: नृ-सिंहैर् नृषु श्रेष्ठैः ॥१८॥ — by the lions of men, the best of men.
18.translation: by the lions of men, the best of men.

19.word_for_word: उपमन्त्रिणः परिहासकाः । — The deputy ministers are ridiculers.; पृथक् पृथक् स्व-स्व-समुदायैः ॥१९॥ — separately in their own communities.
19.translation: The deputy ministers are ridiculers. separately in their own communities.

20.word_for_word: मृदङ्गादयः प्रसिद्धाः । — Mridangas and others are famous.; दरः शङ्खः । — The rate is the conch.; सूतादयस् तुष्टुवुः ॥ — The charioteers and others praised him.; २० ॥ — 20 ॥
20.translation: Mridangas and others are famous. The rate is the conch. The charioteers and others praised him. 20 ॥

21.word_for_word: ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्म वेदम् आहुर् मन्त्रान् व्याचक्षतेत्य् अर्थः । — The Brahmanas say that the Brahman is the Veda, which means that they explain the mantras.; वादिनो वादन-चतुराः ॥ — The players are skilled in playing.; २१-२३ ॥ — 21-23.
21.translation: The Brahmanas say that the Brahman is the Veda, which means that they explain the mantras. The players are skilled in playing. 21-23.

24.word_for_word: गिरि-व्रजे तत् संज्ञके दुर्गे रुद्धा आसन् । — They were confined to a fortress called Tat in Giri-Vraja.; तेषां च दुःखम् आवेदयद् इत्य् अन्वयः ॥२४॥ — and he informed them of their suffering, consequently.
24.translation: They were confined to a fortress called Tat in Giri-Vraja. and he informed them of their suffering, consequently.

25.word_for_word: कृष्ण कृष्ण इति षट्-श्लोकी राज्ञां विज्ञप्तिः, तत्र प्रथमेन शरणाश्रयणं, त्रिभिर् भयानुवादः, द्वाभ्यं प्रार्थनम् इति ॥ — Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, is the six-verse announcement to the kings, in which the first is to take refuge in Him, the third is to explain fear, and the second is to pray.; २५ ॥ — 25 ॥
25.translation: Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, is the six-verse announcement to the kings, in which the first is to take refuge in Him, the third is to explain fear, and the second is to pray. 25 ॥

26.word_for_word:
पृथग्-दर्शिनो लोकस्य भव-भयं विवृण्वन्तो नमन्ति---लोक इति । — Those who see things separately bow down to the world, explaining the fear of its existence.; विकर्म निषिद्धं काम्यं च, तस्मिन् नितरां रतः । — Vikarma is forbidden and desirable, and he is constantly engaged in it.; स्वे कुशले धर्मे पञ्चरात्रे । — In his own good religion, he spent five nights.; सामान्यतश् च गीतासु, — And in general in the Gita,; > यत् करोषि यद् अश्नासि यज् जुहोषि ददासि यत् । — > Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you sacrifice, whatever you give.; >
> यत् तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत् कुरुष्व मद्-अर्पणम् ॥ — >
> Whatever austerities you perform, O son of Kunti, offer them to Me.; [गीता ९.२८] इति > । — [Gita 9.28] It is >.; प्रमत्तोऽनवहितो यावद् अयं लोकस् तावद् एव अस्य लोकस्य यः सद्यो जीविताशां छिनत्ति, तस्मै तुभ्यम् अनिमिषाय कालात्मने नम इति ॥२६॥ — I offer my obeisances unto You, the unblinking Soul of time, who immediately cut off the hope of life of this world as long as this world remains inattentive and uncontrolled.
26.translation:
Those who see things separately bow down to the world, explaining the fear of its existence. Vikarma is forbidden and desirable, and he is constantly engaged in it. In his own good religion, he spent five nights. And in general in the Gita, > Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you sacrifice, whatever you give. >
> Whatever austerities you perform, O son of Kunti, offer them to Me. [Gita 9.28] It is >. I offer my obeisances unto You, the unblinking Soul of time, who immediately cut off the hope of life of this world as long as this world remains inattentive and uncontrolled.

27.word_for_word: सेयं लोकस्य गतिर् वयं तु त्वद्-भक्ताः, अतोऽस्माकं कुत एतद् दुःखम् आपन्नम् ? — That is the way of the world, but we are Your devotees, so where has this suffering come upon us?; इत्य् आश्चर्येणाहुः---लोक इति । — They say, in surprise, that it is the world.; भो ईश ! — Oh, God!; जगत इन ईश्वरः । — The world in God.; त्वयि सद्-रक्षणार्थम् अवतीर्णेऽपि चेद् अस्माकं दुःखं स्यात्, तर्हि किम् अन्यः कश्चिज् जरासन्धादिस् त्वद्-आज्ञाम् अपि लङ्घयति ? — If we were to suffer even when you descended to protect the good, would anyone else, such as Jarasandha, transgress your commands?; किं च, त्वया रक्ष्यमाणोऽपि जनः स्व-कर्म-जं दुःखं प्राप्नोत्य् एवेति न विद्मः । — Moreover, we do not know that even though a person is protected by You, he still suffers the consequences of his own actions.; न चैतद् उभयम् अपि युक्तम् इति भवः ॥२७॥ — Nor is it appropriate for either of these to be the case.
27.translation: That is the way of the world, but we are Your devotees, so where has this suffering come upon us? They say, in surprise, that it is the world. Oh, God! The world in God. If we were to suffer even when you descended to protect the good, would anyone else, such as Jarasandha, transgress your commands? Moreover, we do not know that even though a person is protected by You, he still suffers the consequences of his own actions. Nor is it appropriate for either of these to be the case.

28.word_for_word: किं दुःखं ? — What is the pain?; तद् आहुः---स्वप्नायितम् इति । — They call it a dream.; स्वप्नवज् जातं नृप-सुखं नृपोचितं सुखम् । — It was like a dream, and the king’s happiness was the happiness that a king deserved.; यतः पर-तन्त्रं विषय-साध्यम् । — Because the other system is object-oriented.; किं च, संप्रति शश्वद्-भयं यस्मिन्, तेन मृतक-तुल्येन शरीरेण धुरं पुत्र-दारादि-चिन्तां केवलं वहामः । — What is more, we are only carrying the burden of worrying about our sons, wives and other things with our dead-like bodies in which we are now in eternal fear.; अहो कष्टं नः, ये वयम् इतः पूर्वम् एव निष्कामाः सन्तस् त्वां नाश्रिता इत्य् आहुः---हित्वा इति । — Alas, it is a pity for us, who say that we, who have already been unselfish, have not depended on You, for we have abandoned You.; त्वत् त्वत्तो यद् अनीहैर् निष्कामैर् लभ्यम् आत्मनि स्वतः सिद्धं सुखं तद् धित्वा क्लिश्याम इति ॥२८॥ — That self-perfect happiness in the Self which is obtainable from Thee by those who are free from effort and free from desire, we shall suffer for thinking of it.
28.translation: What is the pain? They call it a dream. It was like a dream, and the king’s happiness was the happiness that a king deserved. Because the other system is object-oriented. What is more, we are only carrying the burden of worrying about our sons, wives and other things with our dead-like bodies in which we are now in eternal fear. Alas, it is a pity for us, who say that we, who have already been unselfish, have not depended on You, for we have abandoned You. That self-perfect happiness in the Self which is obtainable from Thee by those who are free from effort and free from desire, we shall suffer for thinking of it.

29.word_for_word: त्वन्-माया-कृतं कर्म-बन्धं त्वम् एव निवर्तयेति प्रार्थयन्ते--तन् न इति । — They pray that You alone will remove the bondage of karma caused by Your illusory energy, but that is not the case.; वियुङ्क्ष्व मोचय । — Viyunksva Mochaya.; मगधो जरासन्धस् तत्-संज्ञकात् कर्म-पाशात् भवद्भिर् एव विक्रम्य ततो निर्गम्यताम् इति चेद् अत आहुः--य इति । — If it is said that Magadha and Jarasandha should be conquered by you alone and get out of the noose of karma called that, then they say, Ya.; एक एव अयुत-मतङ्गजानां वीर्यं बिभ्रत् सन् स्व-भवने भूभुजोऽस्मान् रुरोध । — The king, carrying the strength of tens of thousands of elephants alone, stopped us in his palace.; सिंहो मेषीर् इव ॥२९॥ — The lion is like a sheep.
29.translation: They pray that You alone will remove the bondage of karma caused by Your illusory energy, but that is not the case. Viyunksva Mochaya. If it is said that Magadha and Jarasandha should be conquered by you alone and get out of the noose of karma called that, then they say, Ya. The king, carrying the strength of tens of thousands of elephants alone, stopped us in his palace. The lion is like a sheep.

30.word_for_word: किं च, युष्मदीया वयम् इत्य् अस्मान् अधिकं बाधत इत्य् आहुः--यो वा इति । — Moreover, they say that it bothers us more that we are yours, or that we are yours.; हे उदात्त-चक्र ! — O noble-wheel!; उद्यत-सुदर्शन ! — Udyat-Sudarshan!; यो वै द्वि-नव-कृत्वोऽष्टादश-वारांस् त्वया सह मृधे वर्तमाने तत्र सप्त-दश-कृत्वस् त्वया खलु भग्नः पराजितः पश्चाद् अनन्त-वीर्यम् अपि नृ-लोके निरतं नर-शरीर-विनोदं भवन्तं सकृज् जित्वा ऊढ-दर्पः प्राप्त-गर्वो युष्मत्-प्रजा नो रुजति पीडयति । — He who has fought with you two or nine times and eighteen times, but you have broken and defeated him seventeen times, and afterwards, even though he has infinite strength, is engaged in the pleasures of the human body in the world of men, he has once defeated you.; तत् तत्र यद् युक्तं तद् विधेहि इत्य् अर्थः ॥३०॥ — That means that you should arrange for whatever is appropriate there.
30.translation: Moreover, they say that it bothers us more that we are yours, or that we are yours. O noble-wheel! Udyat-Sudarshan! He who has fought with you two or nine times and eighteen times, but you have broken and defeated him seventeen times, and afterwards, even though he has infinite strength, is engaged in the pleasures of the human body in the world of men, he has once defeated you. That means that you should arrange for whatever is appropriate there.

35.word_for_word: भूयान् महान् गुणो लाभोऽयम् अस्माकं यत् सर्व-लोक-वृत्तान्त-ज्ञानम् इति ॥ — Our knowledge of the history of the entire universe is a great benefit to us.; ३५ ॥ — 35 ॥
35.translation: Our knowledge of the history of the entire universe is a great benefit to us. 35 ॥

36.word_for_word: ईश्वरः कर्ता येषां, तेषु ॥३६॥ — God is the doer of those, in them.
36.translation: God is the doer of those, in them.

37.word_for_word: एवम् अविदुषेव सर्व-ज्ञेन जरासन्ध-वधार्थम् एव पाण्डव-चिकीर्षितं पृष्टो नारदो मायेयम् इति ज्ञात्वाह---दृष्टा इति त्रिभिः । — Thus, when asked by the omniscient, as if ignorant, what the Pāṇḍavas intended to do was to kill Jarāsandha, Nārada, knowing that it was illusory, replied that he had been seen by three.; विश्व-सृजश् च ब्रह्मणोऽपि मायिनो मोहकस्य ते स्व-शक्तिभिर् विद्यादिभिर् भूतेष्व् अन्तर्यामितया चरतो वर्तमानस्य । — You are the creator of the universe, and you are the illusory, bewildering Brahman, who by His own powers, such as knowledge, moves about in the innermost limits of all living beings.; यद्य् अहं भूतेषु वर्ते तर्हि भूतानि मां किं न पश्यन्ति तत्राह---वह्नेर् इव च्छन्न-रुच इति । — If I exist in beings, then why do not beings see Me?; स्व-शक्तिभिर् एव च्छन्ना रुक् प्रकाशो यस्य तस्य । — The light of the Ruk is covered by its own powers.; अतस् तवेदं प्रश्नादि न मेऽद्भुतम् ॥३७॥ — Therefore your question and others are not surprising to me.
37.translation: Thus, when asked by the omniscient, as if ignorant, what the Pāṇḍavas intended to do was to kill Jarāsandha, Nārada, knowing that it was illusory, replied that he had been seen by three. You are the creator of the universe, and you are the illusory, bewildering Brahman, who by His own powers, such as knowledge, moves about in the innermost limits of all living beings. If I exist in beings, then why do not beings see Me? The light of the Ruk is covered by its own powers. Therefore your question and others are not surprising to me.

38.word_for_word: इदं जगत् । — This is the world.; कथं भूतम् । — How did it happen?; असद् एव यत् तव अचिन्त्यायेत्य् अर्थः ॥३८॥ — This means that whatever is unthinkable to you is unreal.
38.translation: This is the world. How did it happen? This means that whatever is unthinkable to you is unreal.

39.word_for_word: नन्व् एवं-भूतस्य किं माया-चेष्टितैर् इत्य् अत आह---जीवस्येति । — Now, what is the use of the illusory acts of such a being?; अविद्या-तमसा वृतत्वेनानर्थ-प्रापकाच् छरीरात् संसरतः । — Because he is covered by ignorance and darkness, he moves from the body to the source of evil.; तेनैव तपसा तस्माच् छरीराद् विमोक्षोपायम् अजानतः । — By that very austerity, he did not know the means of liberation from that body.; प्राज्वालयत् प्रदीपितवान् । — He lit it and lit it.; तं त्वा त्वाम् । — That’s you, you’re.; यशः श्रवणादिभिर् जीवस्य मोक्षार्थम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३९॥ — This means that fame, hearing and other things are for the sake of liberation of the living entity.
39.translation: Now, what is the use of the illusory acts of such a being? Because he is covered by ignorance and darkness, he moves from the body to the source of evil. By that very austerity, he did not know the means of liberation from that body. He lit it and lit it. That’s you, you’re. This means that fame, hearing and other things are for the sake of liberation of the living entity.

40.word_for_word: आश्रावये श्रावयिष्यामि । — I’ll tell you what I’m telling you.; नर-लोक-विडम्बनं ब्रह्म त्वाम् । — You are the Brahman, the mockery of the human world.; ब्रह्मन्न् इति पाठेऽपि हे ब्रह्मन् परमात्मन्, नर-लोकानुकारिणं त्वां श्रावयिष्यामीति ॥४०-४१॥ — Even in the text, O Brahman, O Supreme Soul, I shall recite to Thee what is beneficial to the world of men (40-41).
40.translation: I’ll tell you what I’m telling you. You are the Brahman, the mockery of the human world. Even in the text, O Brahman, O Supreme Soul, I shall recite to Thee what is beneficial to the world of men (40-41).

42.word_for_word: न चात्रैवानुमोदनं कार्यं, किन्तु तत्रागन्तव्यम् इत्य् आशयेनाह---तस्मिन्न् इति ॥४२॥ — With the intention that approval should not be given here alone, but that it should be reached there, he says, "In that.
42.translation: With the intention that approval should not be given here alone, but that it should be reached there, he says, "In that.

43.word_for_word: तत्रागताश् च सर्वे त्वद्-दर्शनादिना पूता भविष्यन्तीत्य् आह---श्रवणाद् इति । — And all who come there will be purified by seeing You and other things, he says, and by hearing You.; अन्ते-वसायिनः श्व-पचा अपि । — Even the dog-digesters of the end-settlers.; ब्रह्म-मयस्य ब्रह्म-घन-मूर्तेः । — of the Brahma-cube form of the Brahma-maya.; ईक्षा च अभिमर्शः स्पर्शनं च, तौ विद्येते येषाम् ॥४३॥ — Those who have both desire, touch and touch.
43.translation: And all who come there will be purified by seeing You and other things, he says, and by hearing You. Even the dog-digesters of the end-settlers. of the Brahma-cube form of the Brahma-maya. Those who have both desire, touch and touch.

44.word_for_word: कैमुत्यम् अतिशयेनाह---यस्येति । — Kaimutya is exaggerated by the words:---whose.; हे भुवनानां मङ्गल-रूप, दिवि पाताले भूमौ च प्रथितं यस्य यशो विश्वं पुनाति । — O auspicious form of the worlds, whose fame is renowned in heaven, underworld and on earth, it purifies the universe.; कथम् । — How is it.; प्रथितं दिग्-वितानं दिग्-भवनानां वितान-वद् अलङ्करणम् । — The famous directional canopy is decorated like the canopy of the directional buildings.; तथा चरणाम्बु च प्रथितं पुनाति । — Similarly, the water of the feet purifies the well-known.; कथं तत् प्रथितम् । — How is that famous?; दिवि मन्दाकिनीति, अधश् च भोगवतीति, इह च भूमौ गङ्गेति । — In heaven she is called Mandakini, below she is called Bhogavati, and here on earth she is called Ganga.; तस्य तवागमनात् सर्वं मङ्गलं पवित्रं च भविष्यतीति भावः ॥४४॥ — This means that everything will be auspicious and holy by your coming to him.
44.translation: Kaimutya is exaggerated by the words:---whose. O auspicious form of the worlds, whose fame is renowned in heaven, underworld and on earth, it purifies the universe. How is it. The famous directional canopy is decorated like the canopy of the directional buildings. Similarly, the water of the feet purifies the well-known. How is that famous? In heaven she is called Mandakini, below she is called Bhogavati, and here on earth she is called Ganga. This means that everything will be auspicious and holy by your coming to him.

45.word_for_word: तत्रैवं नारदोक्तं तेषु वर्तमानेष्व् आत्मीयम् अक्षेषु यादवेषु जरासन्धस्य विजिगीषया अगृह्णत् स्व-मन्यमानेषु । — There, as Nārada had said, he took his own friend, the Yadavas, who were present in the axes, in order to conquer Jarāsandha, whom he considered to be his own.; वाचः पेशैः पेशल-वाग्भिर् इत्य् अर्थः ॥४५॥ — This means that words are spoken by professionals and by professional words.
45.translation: There, as Nārada had said, he took his own friend, the Yadavas, who were present in the axes, in order to conquer Jarāsandha, whom he considered to be his own. This means that words are spoken by professionals and by professional words.

46.word_for_word: चक्षुष्ट्वे हेतुः, मन्त्रार्थानां मन्त्र-साध्यानां तत्त्व-वित् परिपाक-वेदिता ॥ — The cause of the sight is the knower of the truth and the knower of the cultivation of the objects of the mantras.; ४६-४७ ॥ — 46-47.
46.translation: The cause of the sight is the knower of the truth and the knower of the cultivation of the objects of the mantras. 46-47.
